evidence: Catull. 17.15: puella tenellulō dēlicātior haedō (Lewis & Short: “soft, tender, delicate (poet. and in post-Aug. prose)”)
terms.comment: In this sense, soft or tender, Lewis & Short finds it in poetry and in prose after Augustus; in Cicero it is charming, luxurious, or of persons pampered and fastidious (see particular).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 300, 302.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
